Reference

The Tideglass command reference

Every built-in command, with synopsis, description, and examples. These are the same manual pages the in-shell man command reads — there's … of them. Pipes (|), redirects (> >> <), globs (*), and variables ($VAR, $?) work throughout.

Pipes & redirection

Tideglass parses a real little shell grammar. Commands can be chained with pipes, where the output of one becomes the input of the next, and output can be sent to files:

# count how many lines in the access log were 401s
cat logs/access.log | grep 401 | wc -l

# a sorted, de-duplicated frequency table
cat words.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr

# write and append to files
echo "first line"  >  out.txt
echo "second line" >> out.txt
wc -l < out.txt
Tip: quoting works the way you'd expect. 'single quotes' are literal, "double quotes" still expand $variables, and a backslash escapes the next character.
